transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-02-15 16:00 UTC
Duration: 56 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen, Liam Ortega, Noah Patel (Redwood) - Rachel Torres, Mark Liu, Priya Singh, Ethan Park, Sana Rahman (Cinderpoint)

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, we, uh, we know you had a couple of procurement and legal items to walk through so we thought we'd get the team on. i'm maya, i'm the account exec. liam and noah are here for technical and onboarding.
[00:12] Rachel Torres: thanks maya, appreciate it. big agenda items for us: dpa questions, sla variance on latency for low-latency endpoints, and pricing approvals to enable a pilot.
[00:21] Mark Liu: and InfoSec specifically wants clarity on keying — whether we can bring our own key, hsm, kms, and audit logs. also residency concerns for EU customers.
[00:32] Liam Ortega: sure yes; just to set expectations, we have three deployment modes — hosted api, dedicated reserved capacity, and private (vpc/on-prem). for strong keying we support customer-managed KMS with customer keys, and HSM integrations are on the enterprise/private path. there might be slight perf differences if keys are routed off-site.
[00:50] Priya Singh: on the DPA side, we're seeing some redlines around data retention and deletion timelines, also an indemnity ask tied to model outputs. looking for your standard positions and whether those are negotiable.
[01:05] Maya Chen: yep; typical. we'll send our DPA + controls matrix, that shows SOC2, encryption at rest/in transit, RBAC, audit log retention. on indemnity around outputs we have standard language but we can capture specific examples — usually that's a point for legal review.
[01:19] Ethan Park: can you clarify what 'dedicated' buys us versus 'hosted' in terms of SLA and isolation? our main worry is noisy neighbors and burst capacity during market hours.
[01:30] Liam Ortega: dedicated gives you a reserved GPU pool, predictable throughput and better isolation; we can configure autoscale and burst capacity. SLA tiering improves with dedicated — you can pick a higher SLA and shorter maintenance windows. hosted is simpler and faster to start but shared capacity has co-tenancy risk; we do smart routing but it's not the same as reserved gpus.
[01:52] Sana Rahman: pricing-wise procurement will need a committed number for dedicated to approve. can you give a ballpark for 6-month pilot?
[02:00] Maya Chen: i can share a rough. depends on model size, qps, token count. we'll put a sample costing sheet with token estimates; we also have cost controls — batching, KV cache, quantization — that reduce unit cost.
[02:12] Rachel Torres: on SLAs, our product team wants p95 latency for chat endpoints at < 350ms for certain routes, and p50 at < 120ms. is that realistic on dedicated?
[02:24] Liam Ortega: for those numbers we'd want dedicated in-region low-latency instances; p50 120ms is achievable with optimized runtimes and short seq lengths, p95 350ms is ambitious but doable with warm KV caches and autoscale policies tuned. we'll need to run pilot benchmarks — the distro of sequence lengths matters a lot.
[02:44] Mark Liu: if you promise those in an SLA, what happens on misses? credits? rollback?
[02:50] Maya Chen: standard approach is service credits tied to missed SLO windows; we can map a credit schedule in the SLA. for enterprise contracts we sometimes agree on stepped credits and remediation plans rather than unlimited indemnity.
[03:03] Priya Singh: okay. also we have a requirement that logs and audit trails be retained for 1 year and exportable for our auditors. can you provide export formats and an audit-readout?
[03:14] Noah Patel: yes we expose audit logs via console and S3 export, logs include token-level metadata (not full user data unless flagged) and we can extend retention under enterprise add-on. format is JSON lines; we'll send sample.
[03:27] Rachel Torres: about keying — must our keys never leave our control? We need FIPS-like assurances and HSM-backed signing.
[03:36] Liam Ortega: with Private (VPC/on-prem) you can bring keys that never traverse Redwood-managed control plane; for hosted we offer KMS integration where we keep encrypted blobs but customer-managed keys can be used. HSM on-prem or partner HSM is available under Private enterprise engagements. we'll detail which flows keep keys on-prem.
[03:56] Ethan Park: what about data residency? we need EU-only processing for some customers.
[04:01] Maya Chen: absolutely, we have region pinning — we can enforce processing in eu-central or other regions and have options for Private if you need full physical isolation.
[04:09] Sana Rahman: any egress fees we should account for? our finance team will want to see net cost.
[04:14] Maya Chen: there are standard egress paths; for Dedicated and Private you can reduce egress by colocating or peering. we'll include egress scenarios in the pricing sheet.
[04:23] Priya Singh: milestone timeline — procurement wants the pilot contract signed within three weeks for our board. if legal redlines take longer, that blocks tech testing.
[04:32] Maya Chen: understood — typical flow: we send DPA + MSA defaults and controls now, you send redlines, we review and aim to converge in two-week cycles. parallel to that we'll start pilot planning so tech can bench once legal is comfortable with minimums.
[04:47] Mark Liu: can we get a statement of support for regulatory audits? like a SOC2 report package or SIEM integration notes?
[04:54] Noah Patel: we have SOC2 type II reports, penetration test summaries, and SIEM webhook integrations. i'll attach links.
[05:01] Rachel Torres: on exceptions — one of our stakeholders flagged indemnity caps and data residency carveouts as non-starters — legal will return a list.
[05:09] Priya Singh: yes, we'll share them. also want to confirm you support SAML SSO + SCIM, and RBAC for admin roles.
[05:17] Maya Chen: yes SAML and SCIM supported, RBAC with role templates; for private installs you can map to your identity provider.
[05:24] Ethan Park: pilot scope quick note: 2 endpoints (chat + embeddings), sample throughput 50 qps sustained for 30 minutes, peak bursts to 200 qps, sequence length distribution attached — does that sound reasonable?
[05:36] Liam Ortega: yes that's a good start. we'll produce a benchmark plan with load script, KV cache warmup, and cold-start tests. recommend dedicated for accurate p95 latency measurement.
[05:48] Maya Chen: ok to recap next steps? we'll send DPA + controls matrix and onboarding packet (Maya), liam will send benchmark plan and templated load script, priya will send legal non-starters and indemnity asks, rachel to confirm SLA p50/p95 targets and egress budget.
[06:04] Rachel Torres: sounds good. thanks all.

[06:08] Meeting end.

Notes on transcription: some terms may be misrecognized (e.g., K-V cache -> "K-V cash"), speaker overlap at 03:00 - 03:10, occasional dropped punctuation.
